auditor: Research Alliance for New York City Schools
title: Building School Capacity to Scale Up Computer Science Participation: Insights from NYC’s CS4All Initiative
plain_title: Why some schools got computer science to every student
what_they_audited: A research report from the Research Alliance for New York City Schools, a research center at New York University that studies the city's public schools, on how well individual schools were able to expand computer science under the city's Computer Science for All initiative. It draws on interviews, a school survey and administrative data.
background: Computer Science for All, known as CS4All, launched in 2015 with the goal of giving every student a meaningful computer science experience at least once in each grade band: kindergarten through second grade, third through fifth, sixth through eighth and ninth through twelfth. As the initiative matured it also began helping schools build a broader culture around computer science.

recommendations: Continue emphasizing culture building around computer science in school communities, raising awareness of what it is and how it supports student engagement and learning.

Help schools work through scheduling and staffing obstacles and align computer science with their other instructional priorities, including by fostering communities of practice where school leaders share approaches.
Build connections between computer science instruction and state standards, providing training to map existing curricula onto core content standards or supplying materials already aligned to them.

Target professional learning at the schools furthest behind on participation, including support for building partnerships with outside groups that can supply funding, curricular materials and technology.
